newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt gains on strong T-bond, tempting yields.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt gains on strong T-bond, tempting yields.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices shot up in Thursday's trading session, bolstered by strength in the U.S. Treasuries market, attractive yield spreads and market rumors of new deals and exchanges, traders said.

Brady bonds rose between 3/4 point and one point with Russian debt making substantial gains for the second day. In the U.S. market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury was up 17/32 at 98-09/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
"There's continued strength in the emerging market supported by the U.S. bond rally, optimism about brady exchanges and attractive yield spreads," said one trader.
"Emerging debt prices are providing attractive yields compared to other assets that people can buy," he added.

Russian debt continued to be a key gainer pushing emerging market prices higher, traders said. Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper RUVNUSLNS=RR gained 2-3/4 points to trade at a 68-1/4 bid, after 2-1/2 point gain on Wednesday. The mark-denominated Vnesh RUVNDMLNS=RR bond rose 4-3/8 points to trade at 74 bid.
In Latin America, Argentine labor unions launched a 36-hour general strike on Thursday in their biggest challenge yet to President Carlos Menem's free market reforms.
"It probably has held the market back a little bit," said one trader. "I don't think (Argentina's) strike is that big a deal; their bonds are still up."
Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR rose 7/8 at 59-1/4 bid, while Argentine FRBs ARFLCO5=RR were up 1/8 at 84-1/8.
Meanwhile, Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR gained 1-1/8 points to 71-1/2 bid and Brazilian Pars BR4D24=RR were quoted up 1-1/8 at 60-1/8.

Brazil may issue a $750 million global bond next week consisting of $750 million in five and ten-year maturities, syndicate managers said on Thursday. With little Brazilian debt in the Eurobond market, and no emerging market 10-year dollar bonds, spread talk on the issues was difficult to peg.
"Everyone is extremely interested in this because Brazil is such a rare Euromarket borrower," said one syndicate manager.
In other issues, Peru FLIRBs were quoted up 1-1/2 points to trade at a 52-3/4 while Peru bdi's also traded up at 69 bid, traders said.
